extracted.intended_audience: painters, architectural draughtsmen, art students and critics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for painting architecture and landscape: how to study nature, handle light, age, color, composition, and the relation of human life to architectural subjects. Aimed at producing truthful, expressive, and architecturally plausible works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study from nature; truthful detail in foreground
rubrics_metrics.description: Every fragment of living rock, every tuft of herbage, has manifestations worth recording; a painter who is 'true' need never repeat himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paint foreground details (lichens, herbage, stones, stems, leafage) from direct study of nature rather than inventing 'home inventions' that display perpetual resemblances and repetitions. Avoid relying on stock props (a rutted road, a boggy pool) as compositional crutches; study each stone's lichens and the real forms that occupy the mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance truth of effect with beauty of form and refined color
rubrics_metrics.description: Truth of effect should not be purchased at too great an expense by the loss of all beauty of form and of the higher refinements of color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise thought as well as accuracy of eye—avoid works that are merely exact in appearance but lack considered form and subtle color refinement. Strive for both truthful observation and artistic thoughtfulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid engraving-influenced mannerism; prioritize color and solidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Habitual reference to future translation into light and shade (engraving) can be beneficial for chiaroscuro, but harmful if it fosters dependence on quantity of picturesque material rather than on substantial color or simple treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let the needs of reproduction (engraving, daguerreotype) dictate a loss of solidity, texture, or completeness. Keep substantial color and tactile texture; resist diminishment of size or slightness of execution in pursuit of pictorial effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve sentiment, character, and dignity in subject treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer the impressive to the merely picturesque; avoid coldness of sentiment and trivial choice of subject that yields skies and foliage without story or character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure skies, trees, and foliage convey narrative, dignity, and species-accuracy. Do not sacrifice the dignity of trees for mere wildness; study stems and leafage from nature to retain character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use signs of age judiciously to enhance architectural beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent a building with that amount of age-mark which best exalts and harmonizes its beauty; signs of age can enrich or simplify ornament and often improve effect up to a point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depict weathering, mellow tones, moss, and softened edges where they genuinely enhance the building's character, but avoid substituting crude fractures and blotting stains for fine chiselling and determined color; keep the 'art' of the architecture visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand and employ light, shadow, and aerial perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: The same decoration has totally different effect according to position and time of day; many details must be rendered in 'short-hand' guided by light and shadow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment with steep/level, intense/feeble light; select hinging points revealed by chiaroscuro to explain other parts. Use aerial perspective where appropriate. The real architectural draughtsman varies lighting and chooses salient parts rather than executing everything under one manner or in unintelligible abstracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconcile aerial perspective and chiaroscuro with ornament and gilding
rubrics_metrics.description: Gilded or highly decorated surfaces (as in Venetian painting) must be reconciled with aerial perspective and thoughtfulness of temporary effect to avoid lifelessness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When rendering gold, mosaics, or distant ornament, balance decorative richness with depth, aerial perspective, and chiaroscuro so that splendor does not obliterate solidity or distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance architecture to realization when it is the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: When architecture is central, it must be realized and not treated hastily or as mere background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating architectural elements as vague frames for figures; if the building is the subject, give it substantial form, proportion, and character so it stands as an object of study rather than a suggestive backdrop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mechanical imitation of light-and-shade that erases material and age
rubrics_metrics.description: Mannerisms like violent black ruled lines and slavish imitation of shadow can remove stone texture, fresco records, and colored materials from a representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reduce architecture to uniform dark shadows or 'colored Daguerreotypeism.' Record frescoes, colored marbles, and surface texture; represent materiality and age rather than only blackened chiaroscuro.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convey human life and history through marks on architecture
rubrics_metrics.description: The rent, rust, fissure, lichen, weed, and human inscriptions give architecture its living character and historical meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include signs of habitation, wear, and human inscription in a way that reads as authentic history, not contrived ornament. These marks should deepen the viewer's sense of time and use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finish subordinate parts relative to their function; allow loose execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Subordinate elements may be drawn with 'manly recklessness' so long as the work achieves its intended function and impression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overfinishing every part; subordinate parts may be sketched or 'scrawled' in service of the whole. The degree of finish should be proportional to each element's importance in the composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compose figures naturally within architectural and urban scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be placed so they appear accidental and naturally part of the scene, not posed or merely illustrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place people to contribute to the verisimilitude of streets and markets—figures should feel as if they might move or have agency, not be fixed props. Good figure-placement helps the scene 'breathe.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use luminous, substantial color while maintaining fidelity to detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Color can be sunny and substantial (warm grays, luminous tones), but some palette choices (sandy red, conventional color) can lead to failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for luminous, pure tones where they support the subject; reconcile coloristic brilliance with accurate architectural detail rather than letting color override form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture systemic architectural composition, not only isolated parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Many artists can draw mouldings or windows but fail to 'draw' cathedrals or cities as systems of principal and subordinate parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand and render the architecture's system—principal and subordinate parts in relation—so that even distant 'short-hand' marks preserve the design's discipline and harmony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study figure and drapery from nature; avoid conventional monotone shading
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid violent conventionalism of light and shade and the habit of laying the same arbitrary brown over flesh, dress, or stone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe and study folds and forms from life; vary tonal treatment across surfaces to reflect material and light, rather than applying uniform, conventional shading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fanciful inventions in architectural composition; adhere to architectural truth
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is real beautiful architecture, it is 'treason' to imagine arbitrary monstrous inventions; if composing, design should be such as an architect would applaud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist inventing fantastic cusps, machicolations, or exaggerated decorative bulk for novelty; any compositional invention should respect architectural laws, proportion, and plausibility.
